blocks.text: RNA is usually single-stranded, unlike DNA, but the chain can fold back on itself to form helical loops. A ribonucleotide chain contains ribose, four nitrogenous bases (A, U, G and C; uracil replaces thymine) and phosphate groups. There are three major types of RNA in cells:

items: Messenger RNA (mRNA) carries the genetic blueprint copied from DNA in the nucleus.
Ribosomal RNA (rRNA) helps to make up the ribosome.
Transfer RNA (tRNA) translates the nucleotide sequence of mRNA into the corresponding sequence of amino acids in a protein.

blocks.caption: DNA and RNA compared
rows: carries and translates it (mRNA, tRNA, rRNA)

blocks.prompt: Which base is found in RNA but not in DNA?
blocks.explanation: Uracil (U), which takes the place of thymine.

items: RNA: single strand, ribose, bases A, U, G, C.
mRNA carries the message; rRNA builds ribosomes; tRNA brings amino acids.
